top_categories.workout_context: 629 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 629 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
61,647ft of climbing means repeated surges above threshold. VO2max work is how you survive the fifth climb, not just the first.
At Tour de Suisse Challenge, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Tour de Suisse Challenge's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.
629 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
61,647ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
98ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.
Tour de Suisse Challenge's mixed terrain forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 629 miles.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 61,647ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Tour de Suisse Challenge. Train it until it feels boring.
Low-cadence force work for 61,647ft of climbing. The slow, grinding ascents where you can't spin—you push.

race_overlay.heat: June in Various, Switzerland (last confirmed: full pro Tour de Suisse route, 2023) can bring heat. If the forecast warrants it, include controlled heat exposure before Tour de Suisse Challenge and rehearse the drinking and electrolyte plan you tolerate in training. Do not introduce a fixed sodium protocol solely from this preview.
race_overlay.nutrition: Ultra-distance fueling for 629 miles requires a practiced resupply plan built around confirmed course services and available commercial stops. Rehearse frequent carbohydrate intake on long rides, then scale the plan to intensity, sleep strategy, tolerance, and real food across the full event. Carry redundant fuel and avoid applying a short-event hourly target or fixed total-calorie estimate to a multi-day race.
race_overlay.altitude: Tour de Suisse Challenge with 61,647ft of climbing, much of it above 8,000ft demands altitude preparation. Arrive 5–7 days early for acclimatization. Expect 5–15% power reduction at altitude. Increase iron intake 4 weeks out. Hydrate aggressively — altitude increases fluid loss by 20–40%.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at Tour de Suisse Challenge requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Endurance, and VO2max to prepare you for 629 miles of mixed terrain in Various, Switzerland (last confirmed: full pro Tour de Suisse route, 2023).
